findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' pinned to commit a5d290951de, which is a stray VCS artifact that will make the repository depend on an external nested checkout. CI and any fresh clone will attempt to fetch a nested repository that is not registered in .gitmodules or any known remote, breaking checkout/build for everyone; this is clearly an accidental artifact of the author's local workspace, not part of the feature.

[BUG] The 'upsampled_count' SnQL function is only registered in the discover dataset's function_converter, but the upsampling helper explicitly returns True for the errors dataset, which uses its own function set. When a query runs against the errors dataset (dataset == errors returns True from _should_apply_sample_weight_transform), transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling emits 'upsampled_count() as count', and SnQL query building fails with an unknown-function error, turning a working errors-stats endpoint into a 500 for allowlisted projects.

[BUG] The new SnQL function aggregates Column('sample_weight'), but the diff contains no schema/migration or Snuba column definition establishing that a sample_weight column exists on the events schema; the test factory writes a 'sample_rate' key, not 'sample_weight'. If the events Snuba schema has no sample_weight column, every allowlisted-project query referencing upsampled_count fails at Snuba with an unknown-column error; and even if the test fixtures' client_sample_rate flows to some column, the factory sets 'sample_rate' on normalized_data, so the tests do not actually exercise a sample_weight-backed aggregation.

[BUG] The helper reads options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', []), but no option registration for this key appears anywhere in the diff. If this option is not already registered in sentry/options/defaults.py, sentry's options.get raises for an unregistered key (or silently returns the default with a warning depending on registry state), so the entire eligibility check either crashes or never sees a real allowlist; the diff adds no writer or registration path for it.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined with a docstring saying it 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes', but no caller exists anywhere in the diff. Operators who change the allowlist get stale eligibility for up to 60 seconds per cache key with no way to force invalidation; the shipped function is dead code implying a consistency guarantee that nothing enforces.

[BUG] The producer side of sample_weight/sample_rate exists only in the test factory: no production ingestion/normalizer path in this diff ever sets sample_rate or sample_weight, so the entire upsampling feature is test-only. In production, allowlisted projects' events have no sample_weight column populated, so `upsampled_count()` (sum of NULLs) returns 0 or drops every event — the feature silently returns wrong/zero counts for exactly the allowlisted projects it is gated on, while all diff tests pass because Factories.store_event fabricates the field.

[BUG] sum(sample_weight) silently excludes events whose sample_weight is NULL or 0, so any event stored before the sample_weight backfill (or ingested without the error_sampling context) is dropped from upsampled counts instead of counted as 1. Mixed-population buckets on allowlisted projects undercount: a bucket containing one legacy event reports count 0 (or misses it entirely) where plain count() reported 1 — silent data loss in dashboards/alerts with no error surfaced.

[BUG] In the top-events path only y_axes/timeseries_columns are transformed; self.get_orderby(request) (which resolves to -count() for top events) and self.get_equation_list(request) still reference count(), which no longer exists as an aggregate after the columns are rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count'. A topEvents=5 request on an allowlisted org with orderBy count() issues a SnQL query ordering by an aggregate that is no longer in the projection set, failing the query (500) or producing mis-ranked top events — and no test in the diff exercises the top-events path with upsampling enabled to catch it.

[BUG] invalidate_upsampling_cache() has no caller anywhere in the diff, so the documented 'called when the allowlist configuration changes' contract is unmet and eligibility results are stale for up to 60 seconds after an allowlist change. After removing a project from the allowlist, upsampled (inflated) counts continue to be served for up to 60s on that project's traffic; after adding one, real data is served un-transformed — an operator toggling the option cannot get deterministic behavior from the API despite the helper existing solely for that purpose.

[ADVISORY] The 60s cache is a non-optimization: options.get is an in-process dict lookup (nanoseconds), while the cache adds a Redis roundtrip, an unbounded key space per (org, project-set) tuple, and hash-collision risk since the key uses hash(tuple(...)) rather than the tuple itself. Two distinct (org_id, project_ids) pairs that collide under hash() share one cache entry, so one org's eligible=true flips the other org's query into upsampled counting against a schema it doesn't have — the 'performance optimization' both slows the path and introduces a correctness hazard; deleting the cache layer removes three failure modes at once.

[ADVISORY] Endpoint tests cover only the non-RPC, non-top-events timeseries path; the use_rpc branches (both top-events RPC and plain RPC at lines 229-247 and 273-289 of the endpoint) and the top_events>0 path apply the transform with zero test coverage in this diff. A regression in the RPC or top-events transform wiring (e.g., the orderby mismatch above) ships undetected; self-service users on the RPC dataset path get untransformed or broken counts with no failing test to flag it.

[ADVISORY] _is_error_focused_query treats a discover-dataset query with no event.type filter as non-error, but an unfiltered discover query includes error events, so upsampling is silently skipped for exactly the broadest queries. An org-wide discover chart on an allowlisted org (query='') mixes upsampled false negatives: error counts stay plain count() while the team believes they are viewing upsampled totals, producing inconsistent numbers between the unfiltered chart and the event.type:error chart beside it.

[ADVISORY] The comment claims the eligibility check result 'ensures consistent behavior across query execution', but the cached value only covers the allowlist half — _should_apply_sample_weight_transform re-evaluates per call against a mutable request, so the stated invariant is not what the code provides; a reader relying on the comment will mis-reason about the flag trio (should_upsample / upsampling_enabled / final_columns). The next change to this function (e.g., moving the transform earlier) is built on a false premise about what is cached and consistent, making the flag-trio refactor riskier than it needs to be; the three variables should collapse to one since upsampling_enabled == should_upsample.

[ADVISORY] setUp creates self.user and self.user2 after logging in as self.user, then never uses them; the stored events tag sentry:user with these unrelated users' emails, coupling test setup to dead variables. The next test author extending this class reuses self.user expecting the authenticated user and gets a different user object, producing confusing tag-based assertions; deleting the two user creations (and the user2) removes dead state.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' at commit a5d290951de with no accompanying consumer, build wiring, or explanation anywhere in the diff. Every checkout and CI run now must fetch an unnamed submodule for a feature that references nothing in it; if this was committed accidentally (e.g., a dev's nested checkout), the repo gains a permanent external dependency that breaks shallow clones and pin-mismatch builds.

[BUG] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' (Subproject commit a5d290951de) that is unrelated to error upsampling and referenced by nothing else in the change. Every clone of the repo now requires submodule initialization for an artifact with no consumer; CI and developers fail or pull unrelated code, and the submodule pin silently rots. This is work not traceable to any requirement in the PR title or any call site in the diff.

[BUG] The 'upsampled_count' SnQL function is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter, but the helper routes errors-dataset queries through the same transform, which emits 'upsampled_count() as count' for dataset == errors. Any query against the errors dataset (sentry.snuba.errors) for an allowlisted org sends an unregistered function to SnQL parsing and fails with a query-parse error (500) instead of returning counts; the tests only exercise the discover dataset, so this path ships broken. Under-scoped implementation: the transform's dataset gate (error_upsampling.py lines 96-98, 'if dataset == errors: return True') is inconsistent with where the function exists.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash() of a tuple ('hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))'), which is randomized per process via PYTHONHASHSEED. The key differs between worker processes and between runs, so (a) the '60s performance optimization' cache almost never hits across processes, defeating its stated purpose, and (b) invalidate_upsampling_cache computes a different key than the one a given worker wrote, so it never invalidates the right entry. The caching layer is dead weight that only adds a Redis round-trip.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code with no caller in this diff, and even if called it cannot work: the cache key embeds the exact sorted project-id tuple, so an allowlist change cannot enumerate and clear the unbounded set of org/project-combination keys. The docstring claims 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency', but no writer of the allowlist option exists in the diff and the invalidation is structurally impossible for any combination not passed in; operators cannot actually enforce allowlist removal within the 60s TTL. Ships-inert feature plus a misleading contract.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint now makes an unconditioned eligibility check (cache lookup + potential allowlist option read) on every stats request, including queries for orgs/projects with nothing to do with upsampling, and the result is aliased through two variables ('should_upsample' then 'upsampling_enabled') that are never distinct. A global hot path (org events-stats serves all dashboards/alerts) gains a per-request cache round-trip and option read for the vast majority of traffic where the answer is False; the duplicated aliasing and three re-application branches (lines 224-230, 275-277, 294-296) mean the next change to the transform must be threaded through three call sites, increasing drift risk. Simplification: compute final_columns once before the branch split.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated user-facing error-message fix ('If topEvents needs to be at least 1' -> 'topEvents needs to be at least 1') rides along in the upsampling PR. Unrelated churn in a performance/feature PR: it confuses blame and bisect and has no test; should be a separate trivial change. Work not traceable to the stated intent.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling swallows all exceptions with bare 'except Exception: pass' twice, and store_event (shared by every test in the suite) now mutates normalized_data based on an optional context key for all event types, not just error-sampled ones. Malformed contexts.error_sampling payloads are silently ignored with no signal, and any future test storing a 'sample_rate' field for unrelated reasons gets it overwritten from contexts, producing hard-to-debug cross-test coupling. A narrower transform (only when the key exists, no broad except) would avoid both.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling emits `upsampled_count() as count` for errors-dataset queries, but the SnQL function `upsampled_count` is only registered in the discover dataset's function_converter (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1041), so any errors-dataset query that gets transformed references an unregistered function. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, so every errors-dataset events-stats request for an allowlisted project produces a query with an unknown aggregate and fails (SnQL parse/execution error -> 500) instead of returning stats.

[BUG] The factory helper writes `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`, but the upsampling aggregation sums `Column("sample_weight")`, and no production ingest/relay/consumer path in this diff (or referenced anywhere) writes a sample_weight value for errors. The only writer of the source value is test-only (sentry/testutils/factories.py), so the feature is inert in production: for allowlisted projects, upsampled_count() sums a column nothing populates, yielding 0/null counts on real data while tests pass because the factory fakes the value.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring test (`"event.type:error" in query`) on the lowercased query string, so any query containing that substring anywhere — including a negation like `!event.type:error` or a filter on a different field mentioning it — is classified as error-focused. On the discover dataset, a transaction query that negates event.type:error gets sum(sample_weight) applied to transaction rows, inflating counts (or failing on a missing sample_weight column) for allowlisted projects instead of returning plain count().

[BUG] An empty or unfiltered query on the discover dataset — which queries error events by default in this endpoint — returns False from _is_error_focused_query, so upsampling is silently skipped for the most common discover stats query shape. For allowlisted projects, GET /events-stats with no event.type filter (the default dashboard/issue-stats pattern) returns un-upsampled count() while the same org with `event.type:error` appended returns upsampled counts, so the two views of the same data disagree by the sampling factor.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller in this diff and, because the allowlist is a single global option while the cache key is per-org-per-project-set, it cannot invalidate the existing entries when the option changes. When an operator edits the allowlist, every previously-issued (org, project-set) cache key remains stale for up to its TTL; the dead invalidation function gives a false sense of consistency and the next maintainer wiring it up will discover it cannot enumerate keys.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only the exact string `count()` (case/whitespace-insensitive); aliased forms (`count() as total`) and other counting aggregates (count_if, count_unique, count_microsoft…) pass through untransformed. A top-events request whose yAxis or equations use any counting variant other than bare `count()` silently mixes weighted and unweighted numbers in one response — the next contributor extending the transform has to rediscover every spelling, and users see inconsistent magnitudes across columns of the same chart.

[ADVISORY] The column transformation is applied to y_axes/timeseries_columns only; orderby, equations, and groupby strings still contain the original count() references, so transformed and untransformed aggregates coexist within a single top-events query. Top-events ordering (orderby count()) ranks groups by raw sampled count while the returned series shows the weighted count, so the displayed order can contradict the displayed magnitudes for sampled projects.

[ADVISORY] The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))` and a bare 60-second TTL literal, and _are_all_projects_error_upsampled never validates that the allowlisted project ids belong to the passed organization despite taking it as a parameter. The TTL constant has no named provenance so future copies will diverge silently, and the unused organization parameter signals a tenant check that does not exist — the global allowlist is trusted for any project id the caller supplies.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps field extraction and conversion in bare `except Exception: pass` blocks, so a malformed contexts payload is silently ignored with no signal. A test fixture with a typo'd key (e.g. client_sample_rat) silently produces an event with no sample_rate, and the resulting upsampled-count assertions fail with a confusing 1-vs-10 mismatch instead of a clear setup error.

[BUG] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, so the cache-invalidation path the design promised does not exist and allowlist changes are not picked up until the 60-second TTL expires. When an operator adds a project to the allowlist, that project's error counts continue to be reported as raw count() (un-upsampled) for up to 60 seconds per (org, project-set) key; the docstring's claim 'This should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' is unfulfilled intent — the function is ships-inert, and any future caller would have to know the exact cache-key format including hash(tuple(...)) to construct the key, which is a hidden coupling.

[BUG] The user-facing error message for topEvents<=0 was silently reworded ('If topEvents needs to be at least 1' -> 'topEvents needs to be at least 1') with no connection to the stated upsampling intent. This is an unreviewed objective change smuggled into the feature PR: any client or test matching on the prior error string (e.g. Sentry's own frontend or SDK integration tests asserting the 'If topEvents' wording) breaks, and reviewers accepting 'upsampling support' never explicitly accepted an API error-message change.

[BUG] A new git submodule 'sentry-repo' pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a was added, which is unrelated to the upsampling feature and looks like an accidental working-tree artifact. Merging this pins an unreviewed submodule into the repository — every clone will fetch an extra tree, CI that checks out submodules pulls unvetted code, and the intent of the PR ('support upsampled error count') was never stated to include adding a nested repository.

[BUG] The cached path caches only the allowlist check but the code path semantics drifted from the docstring: the 60s-cached eligibility means the 'consistent behavior across query execution' claim is false, and the _are_all_projects_error_upsampled NOTE claiming 'we always have the latest configuration state' is directly contradicted by the cache added above it. Within a single rolling window, the same (org, project-set) query flips between upsampled counts (10x inflated) and raw counts after an allowlist edit, producing visibly discontinuous timeseries for dashboard users; the two docstrings in the same file assert opposite consistency guarantees, so at least one documented intent is not what the code does.

[ADVISORY] The new production module sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling and its test module were both added to what appears to be a per-module ignore/exclusion list (the same list as other api helpers), changing the lint/coverage constraint surface without comment. The next engineer adding logic to error_upsampling.py inherits whatever exclusion was granted here (e.g. skipped typing or coverage enforcement) without realizing this PR negotiated it; this is a silent loosening of accepted repo constraints bundled inside a feature PR.

[ADVISORY] setUp reassigns self.user after login_as(self.user) and stores the original in a non-standard self.authed_user, silently swapping the authenticated identity for the logged-in session. Every test in this class authenticates as the original user while self.user now refers to a different, never-logged-in user; the next person copying this setUp pattern (or asserting on self.user's audit/ownership behavior) gets surprising results, and the drift from the file's existing setUp conventions was not part of the feature's stated intent.

[ADVISORY] The transformation is now applied in three duplicated call sites (top_events RPC, top_events non-RPC, plain RPC, plain non-RPC — four total) instead of once on query_columns before branching, with the 'final_columns = query_columns' pre-assignment plus per-branch re-transformation leaving dead/redundant work in the top_events branch. The next change to column handling (e.g. adding equation support or a fourth query path) must remember to thread final_columns through each of four branches; a missed branch silently serves un-upsampled counts to allowlisted projects, which the existing structure invites rather than prevents.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query matches the raw substring 'event.type:error' in the user's query string, so negated or OR-combined queries that do NOT scope to errors (e.g. '!event.type:error', 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction') are classified as error-focused and get the sum(sample_weight) transform applied to rows that have no sample_weight. A discover-dataset query that excludes or mixes non-error events returns counts computed from sum(sample_weight) over transactions rows where sample_weight is absent/null, producing silently wrong (zero or inflated) counts for the user's chart.

[BUG] The cache key embeds Python's hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))), whose value is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the key written by is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects in one process never matches the key deleted by invalidate_upsampling_cache in another, making invalidation a no-op. After the allowlist changes, every process keeps serving its own 60-second cached eligibility decision (including stale 'eligible' results that apply the upsampled count transform to projects no longer allowlisted), and the documented invalidation contract silently fails cluster-wide.

[ADVISORY] The code establishes a trust-the-client path where sample_rate is derived directly from the SDK-supplied contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate, and upsampled_count() aggregates sum(sample_weight) built on that value. Any client can report an arbitrary client_sample_rate (e.g. 1e9), and if this pattern is carried into production ingestion the upsampled error counts the API returns become attacker-controlled multipliers — inflated or deflated error statistics for dashboards and alerting built on this endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The test file never exercises is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — the only function the endpoint actually calls — leaving its entire cache layer (key construction, cache.set/get, the 'cached_result and _should_apply...' composition) with zero coverage. A regression in the caching logic (e.g. returning the cached bool without the dataset check, or an inverted cache write) passes the whole new test suite; the unit tests only cover the private helpers, so the composition the production code depends on is verified nowhere.

[ADVISORY] All four endpoint tests mock the options module wholesale (mock.patch of sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options), so the option name string 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' is never validated against a registered option. A typo in the option key inside error_upsampling.py (e.g. 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlst') passes every test in this diff because Mock.get returns the allowlist for any key; in production options.get would return the default and upsampling would silently never activate.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint tests exercise only the standard non-top-events discover path; the top_events>0 branch and both use_rpc branches in _get_event_stats — three of the four code paths that apply transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling — are never triggered by any test in the diff. A bug where the transformation is applied in one branch but not another (e.g. final_columns computed but the run_top_events_timeseries_query call still passing the original y_axes) ships undetected, producing undercounted charts on dashboards using topEvents or RPC mode.

[ADVISORY] test_should_apply_sample_weight_transform verifies the errors-dataset branch only via a direct module-object call, and no endpoint test ever issues a request with dataset=errors, so the errors-dataset eligibility path is untested end-to-end. If the endpoint wiring passes a different dataset object (e.g. a wrapped/aliased dataset module that fails the 'dataset == errors' identity comparison), all error queries silently fall back to plain count(); no test in the diff would catch it because the e2e tests only ever hit the discover branch.

[ADVISORY] test_transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only covers bare 'count()' variants and never tests a column with an existing alias such as 'count() as total', which the implementation rewrites to 'upsampled_count() as count', silently discarding the caller's alias. The test table only contains inputs the implementation already special-cases (mirror-test shape); any caller passing aliased count columns gets the alias renamed to 'count' with no test failing, breaking downstream consumers that select by the original alias.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff and no test, so the documented cache-invalidation contract is unimplemented and unverifiable. Operators changing the allowlist wait out the 60-second TTL per org/project-key combination (and in multi-region deployments the cache is per-process), so newly allowlisted projects serve unupsampled counts and newly de-allowlisted projects serve inflated upsampled counts with no code path to correct it; the function's existence in the diff creates false confidence that invalidation happens.

[ADVISORY] setUp reassigns self.user and self.user2 via create_user() after login_as(self.user), so the user authenticated in the test client is not the object the tests later reference, and the event tags 'sentry:user' embed a user created after login. The test still passes because the session was established before reassignment, but any future assertion touching self.user (e.g. per-user event stats) silently asserts against a different user than the one logged in, a latent trap for the next test added to this class.

[BUG] The new upsampled_count aggregation sums sample_weight, but this diff contains no migration or backfill that guarantees sample_weight is populated for existing/historical error rows in the Snuba events schema, so pre-sampling-rollout events return sum = 0 (or the column default) instead of a count of 1. As soon as a project is added to the allowlist, every time bucket whose events predate sample_weight population reports count 0 instead of the true count — the org's error stats silently drop to zero with no error surfaced, and there is no backfill step in this diff to repair it.

[BUG] A git submodule pointer 'sentry-repo' at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a is introduced in this diff with no corresponding .gitmodules entry, so the tree state that the code (and any migration-related vendored content) depends on cannot be reproduced by checkout. CI/other checkouts get an empty or unresolvable path (git submodule update fails with no .gitmodules URL), so the reviewed state is not actually deployable; if any schema/backfill artifacts were meant to live there, they are silently missing.

[ADVISORY] The transformation relies on a Snuba-side sample_weight column whose rollout is not represented anywhere in this diff (no migration, no feature flag gating on schema readiness), creating an untracked cross-system schema dependency: app code ships expecting a column the storage layer may not have on all clusters. During the window where the Snuba schema has not been updated on a region, every allowlisted query raises an unknown-column error from Snuba, breaking the events-stats endpoint for those orgs until the storage side catches up — with no rollback short of removing the allowlist entries.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache keys on the exact set of project_ids, so a dashboard issuing the same org query with differing project subsets populates unbounded cache entries, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() (which no caller in this diff invokes) only deletes one exact key combination. After an allowlist change, orgs keep the stale eligible/ineligible decision for up to 60s per distinct project-set key (the invalidate helper is dead code in this diff), yielding inconsistent counts between adjacent chart panels; the next change to this feature must account for key combinatorics the helper cannot clear.

[ADVISORY] The factory backfill copies client_sample_rate into sample_rate only when the field is present in contexts, with bare except swallowing both missing and unparseable values, so test fixtures silently produce events with no sample_rate — mirroring exactly the production backfill gap that makes upsampled_count return 0 for old events. Future tests written against fixtures lacking the contexts field will exercise the upsampled path with null sample_weight and assert on 0-counts, baking the data-loss failure mode into the test suite rather than exposing it.

[BUG] upsampled_count() computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/default, so any event row where sample_weight is NULL or 0 (events stored before the rollout, or stored without an error_sampling context since nothing backfills it) contributes nothing or NULL to the sum. For an allowlisted project with pre-existing events, the timeseries returns count of 0 (toInt64(NULL) = 0) for buckets that actually contain errors — the API reports success while silently dropping real counts, and dashboards show missing/out-of-nowhere data when the allowlist flips on.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the literal string count(); every other count-bearing aggregate (count_if(...), count_msr(...), epm(), and count() embedded with an alias like 'count() as total') is passed through unweighted. A single response can mix weighted (upsampled) and unweighted (raw sampled) series — e.g. yAxis count() is multiplied by 10 while a second yAxis epm() or an aliased count() stays raw-sampled — silently presenting inconsistent magnitudes as one successful result with no error or flag.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code — no caller exists in this diff (no writer path updates the allowlist and invalidates), and even if called it could not work: the cache key embeds hash(sorted(project_ids)), so every distinct project subset the API ever receives creates its own key that no invalidation call can enumerate. An operator flips a project off the allowlist and for up to 60 seconds every cached (org, project-subset) key continues serving eligibility=True, inflating counts by the stale sample factor on a user-facing chart; the provided invalidation function gives a false sense of a consistency mechanism that can never fire correctly.

[ADVISORY] The cache key uses Python's hash() on a tuple of ints, which is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same (organization, projects) pair produces different keys in different processes and across restarts. The 'performance optimization' cache is effectively per-worker and cold after every deploy/restart, so under traffic the claim it optimizes for (avoiding repeated lookups across the fleet) does not hold; collision between distinct (org, project-subset) tuples sharing a hash bucket would return the wrong eligibility, though that probability is negligible.

[ADVISORY] The upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered without private=True, making it a user-selectable aggregate in discover/tagstone queries on any dataset and any project, allowlisted or not. A user can run upsampled_count() against a non-allowlisted project or the transactions/spans datasets and get sum(sample_weight) over data where the weight semantics don't apply (missing weights → 0/NULL per the function body), receiving confidently wrong numbers in a successful 200 response with nothing indicating the function is unsupported there.

[ADVISORY] The eligibility check runs unconditionally at the top of _get_event_stats on every request, including pure transactions/spans queries where _should_apply_sample_weight_transform can never return True, and the eligibility result is cached under a key that does not include the dataset or query — only the allowlist half is cached while the dataset/query half is recomputed. Every non-error stats request pays a cache round-trip for a decision that is always False for it (added hot-path work on the previously unguarded path), and the cache-hit fast path `cached_result and _should_apply_...` still re-executes the dataset dispatch each call, so the caching structure optimizes the cheap half (an options.get) while leaving the dispatch uncached.

[ADVISORY] _is_error_focused_query checks only the raw 'query' GET param for the substring event.type:error; a discover-dataset request whose query is rewritten/enriched upstream (or which filters errors via other means, e.g. no event.type filter at all, which on the discover dataset returns a mix including errors) is misclassified. On the discover dataset with no explicit event.type:error token (e.g. the default stats chart querying a mixed or error-only-by-context stream), the transform is silently skipped and the chart shows raw sampled counts while the same org+projects with the token added shows 10x counts — two views of the same data disagree with no error surfaced.

goldens.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The transformation relies on a Snuba-side sample_weight column whose rollout is not represented anywhere in this diff (no migration, no feature flag gating on schema readiness), creating an untracked cross-system schema dependency: app code ships expecting a column the storage layer may not have on all clusters. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache keys on the exact set of project_ids, so a dashboard issuing the same org query with differing project subsets populates unbounded cache entries, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() (which no caller in this diff invokes) only deletes one exact key combination. After an allowlist change, orgs keep the stale eligible/ineligible decision for up to 60s per distinct project-set key (the invalidate helper is dead code in this diff), yielding inconsistent counts between adjacent chart panels; the next change to this feature must account for key combinatorics the helper cannot clear.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects()` which caches eligibility under `cache_key = f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"` (new `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] upsampled_count() computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/default, so any event row where sample_weight is NULL or 0 (events stored before the rollout, or stored without an error_sampling context since nothing backfills it) contributes nothing or NULL to the sum. For an allowlisted project with pre-existing events, the timeseries returns count of 0 (toInt64(NULL) = 0) for buckets that actually contain errors — the API reports success while silently dropping real counts, and dashboards show missing/out-of-nowhere data when the allowlist flips on.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `upsampled_count` in `discover.function_converter` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` for allowlisted projects. There is no handling for missing/NULL `sample_weight` (no `coalesce`, `ifNull`, or fallback to 1), and `error_upsampling.py` explicitly assumes the column “exists for all events” rather than enforcing it. If `sample_weight` is NULL for a bucket (e.g., older events or events without that field populated), `sum(sample_weight)` can be NULL/0 and the API will return 0 counts despite events existing, silently undercounting. This is a correctness defect introduced by the new aggregation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the literal string count(); every other count-bearing aggregate (count_if(...), count_msr(...), epm(), and count() embedded with an alias like 'count() as total') is passed through unweighted. A single response can mix weighted (upsampled) and unweighted (raw sampled) series — e.g. yAxis count() is multiplied by 10 while a second yAxis epm() or an aliased count() stays raw-sampled — silently presenting inconsistent magnitudes as one successful result with no error or flag.

adjudication.rationale: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, only the exact normalized string `"count()"` is rewritten (`if column_lower == "count()": ...`). Any other count-derived aggregation (e.g. `count_if(...)`, `epm()`) or `count()` with an alias like `"count() as total"` will pass through unchanged. In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, when `upsampling_enabled` is true, it applies this transform to the full `query_columns` list, so a multi-yAxis request can produce a response where one series is upsampled (via `upsampled_count()`) while others remain raw-sampled, yielding inconsistent magnitudes with no warning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code — no caller exists in this diff (no writer path updates the allowlist and invalidates), and even if called it could not work: the cache key embeds hash(sorted(project_ids)), so every distinct project subset the API ever receives creates its own key that no invalidation call can enumerate. An operator flips a project off the allowlist and for up to 60 seconds every cached (org, project-subset) key continues serving eligibility=True, inflating counts by the stale sample factor on a user-facing chart; the provided invalidation function gives a false sense of a consistency mechanism that can never fire correctly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, but there is no caller introduced anywhere in this PR, so within this diff it is unused/dead code. Also, the cache key is computed as `error_upsampling_eligible:{org_id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`, meaning eligibility is cached per (org, exact project-id-set). If the allowlist changes for a project, invalidating only one specific `(org, project_ids)` tuple would not invalidate other cached subsets that include that project; the diff shows no mechanism to enumerate/clear all such keys. This is a concrete maintainability/consistency concern created by the new caching approach, though the 60s staleness is an explicit design tradeoff in the docstring rather than a provable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache key uses Python's hash() on a tuple of ints, which is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same (organization, projects) pair produces different keys in different processes and across restarts. The 'performance optimization' cache is effectively per-worker and cold after every deploy/restart, so under traffic the claim it optimizes for (avoiding repeated lookups across the fleet) does not hold; collision between distinct (org, project-subset) tuples sharing a hash bucket would return the wrong eligibility, though that probability is negligible.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, the cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Using Python’s built-in `hash()` makes the key process-dependent (hash randomization via `PYTHONHASHSEED`), so if `cache` is shared across workers (as Sentry typically configures), different processes will generate different keys for the same project set and the cache won’t be effective fleet-wide and will be cold after restarts/deploys. Also, using only a hash of the project-id tuple introduces a (very small) possibility of collisions between different project sets, which could yield an incorrect cached eligibility result. This is a real, diff-grounded concern but more about caching design/performance/robustness than a guaranteed functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered without private=True, making it a user-selectable aggregate in discover/tagstone queries on any dataset and any project, allowlisted or not. A user can run upsampled_count() against a non-allowlisted project or the transactions/spans datasets and get sum(sample_weight) over data where the weight semantics don't apply (missing weights → 0/NULL per the function body), receiving confidently wrong numbers in a successful 200 response with nothing indicating the function is unsupported there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The eligibility check runs unconditionally at the top of _get_event_stats on every request, including pure transactions/spans queries where _should_apply_sample_weight_transform can never return True, and the eligibility result is cached under a key that does not include the dataset or query — only the allowlist half is cached while the dataset/query half is recomputed. Every non-error stats request pays a cache round-trip for a decision that is always False for it (added hot-path work on the previously unguarded path), and the cache-hit fast path `cached_result and _should_apply_...` still re-executes the dataset dispatch each call, so the caching structure optimizes the cheap half (an options.get) while leaving the dispatch uncached.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, the diff adds an unconditional call at the top: `should_upsample = is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` (before any branching on dataset/query). That helper always performs a cache lookup (`cache.get(cache_key)`) and on miss may `options.get(...)` and `cache.set(...)`, even for datasets where upsampling can never apply (e.g., `transactions` in `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`). Also, the cache key in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` only includes org id and project ids, not dataset nor request query, and the cache-hit path still recomputes `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` every call (`cached_result and _should_apply...`). This is a real performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, but it does not demonstrate a correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _is_error_focused_query checks only the raw 'query' GET param for the substring event.type:error; a discover-dataset request whose query is rewritten/enriched upstream (or which filters errors via other means, e.g. no event.type filter at all, which on the discover dataset returns a mix including errors) is misclassified. On the discover dataset with no explicit event.type:error token (e.g. the default stats chart querying a mixed or error-only-by-context stream), the transform is silently skipped and the chart shows raw sampled counts while the same org+projects with the token added shows 10x counts — two views of the same data disagree with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` only enables the transform for the `discover` dataset when `_is_error_focused_query(request)` returns True, and `_is_error_focused_query` is implemented as a simple substring check for `"event.type:error"` in the raw `request.GET["query"]` (see `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`). This means discover queries that effectively target errors without that exact token (or if the effective query differs from the raw GET param) will skip upsampling and can yield different counts depending on whether the token is present. The diff itself doesn’t prove the upstream rewriting/default-chart behavior claimed, but it does show a concrete, potentially inconsistent edge-case created by this heuristic.
